FARRA:v3p251/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p251/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p251/r7.claim: Wa-saqa means what the night gathered.

TAB-FULL:v24p244/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p244/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p244/r1.claim: The oath pairs the departing day with the arriving night. Al-Ṭabarī prefers shafaq as the day as it recedes; in the legal timing of ʿIshāʾ, shafaq means redness, as he explains in his book on prayer.

TAB-FULL:v24p245/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p245/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p245/r1.claim: Wasq means gathering; the oath covers what night gathers among creatures that settle, fly, or crawl after daytime. The root also describes collected food in a container, and a wasq is sixty ṣāʿs.

TAB-FULL:v24p245/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p245/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p245/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “what it gathers” as whatever night collects, and cites a poetic line about creatures crowded together if they had a herder.

TAB-FULL:v24p245/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p245/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p245/r3.claim: Mujāhid says it is whatever the night gathers or shelters, including creatures it contains; he also glosses the phrase as what it folds or covers.

TAB-FULL:v24p245/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p245/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p245/r4.claim: Qatāda says the night gathers stars or animals.

TAB-FULL:v24p245/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p245/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p245/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says it is whatever God gathers in the night: creatures that shelter there and things occurring at night but not during the day.

TAB-FULL:v24p247/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p247/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p247/r1.claim: Mujāhid also glosses wasaq as what entered the night or what it covered and drew together.

TAB-FULL:v24p247/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p247/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v24p247/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says it is whatever the night gathers.

TAB-FULL:v24p247/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p247/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p247/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says it is what night encloses, or what it drives as darkness and sends each thing toward its shelter.

TAB-FULL:v24p247/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p247/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p247/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the night brings darkness along as it arrives.

ZAJJAJ:v5p305/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p305/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p305/r2.claim: Wasaqa means gathered and joined together; a poet’s mustawsiqāt illustrates things gathered together.

NAHHAS:v5p185/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r24.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p185/r24.claim: The wāw is conjunctive, not an oath particle.

THALABI:v10p160/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p160/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p160/r11.claim: Wasq means gathering or collecting; a wasq of food is a large collected measure of sixty sāʿ, and mawsaq food is gathered in a sack or vessel.

THALABI:v10p160/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p160/r12.speaker: مجاهد برواية ابن أبي بحج
THALABI:v10p160/r12.claim: He interprets what the night gathers as the animals it shelters.

THALABI:v10p160/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p160/r13.speaker: منصور
THALABI:v10p160/r13.claim: He says the night folds over and darkens what it contains, and things enter into it.

THALABI:v10p160/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p160/r14.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v10p160/r14.claim: He interprets it as the animals, scorpions, snakes, and darkness the night gathers.

THALABI:v10p160/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p160/r15.speaker: ضحاك ومقاتل
THALABI:v10p160/r15.claim: They say night brings its darkness, and creatures then go to their shelters.

THALABI:v10p160/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p160/r16.speaker: الأستاذ أبو القاسم بن حبيب
THALABI:v10p160/r16.claim: He suggests that the explanation involving sāqa may be an inversion, since the basic verb is sāqa yasūqu.

THALABI:v10p160/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p160/r17.speaker: عثمان
THALABI:v10p160/r17.claim: He interprets the phrase as the load of darkness.

THALABI:v10p160/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p160/r18.speaker: أبو حيان
THALABI:v10p160/r18.claim: He explains it as the arrival of darkness or a star.

THALABI:v10p160/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p160/r19.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p160/r19.claim: He interprets the phrase as what a person does during the night.

THALABI:v10p160/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p160/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p160/r20.claim: He says the night gathers things, and appeals to a line of poetry using مستوسقات for collected camels.

THALABI:v10p161/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p161/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p161/r1.claim: A poetic line uses مستوسقات of gathered camels as evidence for wasq meaning collected together.

QUSHAYRI:v3p405/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p405/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p405/r10.claim: The night gathers and encloses what it covers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r1.speaker: مجاهد ومسروق والحسن وأبو صالح وأبو العالية وابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r1.claim: They interpret wa-saq as what night gathered, enclosed, collected, or folded; a report from Ibn Abbas gives gathered.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r2.speaker: الفراء والزجاج والمبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r2.claim: They prefer the meaning gathered, supported by a poetic phrase for gathered animals.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r3.claim: Wa-saq is related to a measured load because it gathers a known amount; at night creatures return to shelter, gathering what was dispersed in daytime.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r4.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r4.claim: Wasq means joining things together; camels are said to gather, and a herdsman gathers them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r5.claim: He says the night drives things to where they shelter; on this reading wasq means driving, as in a drove of animals.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r6.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p365/r6.claim: He reads wa-saq as what the night carries; carrying here means gathering and enclosing all the trees, mountains, seas, and earth in darkness.

JISHUMI:v10p7342/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7342/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7342/r10.claim: Wasaq means gathering; it can also name the collected load of food, measured at sixty ṣāʿs.

JISHUMI:v10p7342/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7342/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7342/r11.claim: His poetic citation uses mustawsiqāt for gathered-together things.

JISHUMI:v10p7342/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7342/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7342/r12.claim: He says wasaq can mean driving or carrying in Arabic, and means driving in this verse.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r6.claim: وسق means gathered and joined; as night comes, creatures spread by day return to their shelters.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r7.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r7.claim: Mansur reports Mujahid’s gloss: what night folded over and darkened.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r8.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r8.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan explains it as the arrival of darkness or a star.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r9.claim: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr says it means what was done during the night.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458#2/r6.claim: Wasaqa means gathered and joined; a wasq is a heap of gathered measures.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458#2/r7.claim: Night gathers animals and all earthly and atmospheric creatures, including seas, mountains, and winds.

TABRISI:84:13-19/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:13-19/r10.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
TABRISI:84:13-19/r10.claim: They read wasaq as what the night drives toward its dwelling, since darkness moves things into their homes.

TABRISI:84:13-19/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:13-19/r11.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:84:13-19/r11.claim: Abu Muslim says the phrase refers to stars driven into view by night and hidden by day.

TABRISI:84:13-19/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:13-19/r9.speaker: عكرمة وغيره
TABRISI:84:13-19/r9.claim: “What the night gathers” means all that was dispersed during the day returning to its shelter.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:17-19/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17-19/r13.speaker: ابن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17-19/r13.claim: He says the night gathers what people do in it, including night prayer and seeking forgiveness before dawn; a poem compares it to work.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r1.claim: Wasq means gather, enclose, and wrap; night gathers what was scattered during the day, as mountains, trees, seas, and land are covered.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r10.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r10.claim: Carrying means gathering and enclosing: darkness covers everything, so the oath includes all creatures.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r2.claim: They explain the night as gathering and enclosing things; the discussion links this to God's making night for rest and day for seeking bounty.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r3.speaker: ضابيء بن الحارث البرجمي
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r3.claim: His poem compares helpless longing to grasping water, which illustrates how the night gathers what it covers.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r4.claim: Wasq is joining things together; a wasq is a large gathered quantity of food equal to sixty ṣāʿ.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r5.claim: Mawsūq means collected and mustawsiq camels are gathered together; a rajaz poem uses the latter word.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r6.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r6.claim: He says the night drives things to where they take shelter; wasīqah names a herd driven along as prey.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r7.claim: He also glosses what the night gathers as what it conceals and covers.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r8.claim: Another gloss is what the night carries; Arabic speakers say 'as long as my eye carried water,' and camels or palms can carry loads or fruit.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r9.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
QURTUBI-FULL:84:17/r9.claim: He interprets the carried thing as darkness, or, in another statement, the stars.

BAYDAWI-FULL:84:13-19/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:13-19/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:13-19/r3.claim: The night gathers and conceals creatures and other things, or drives them to their places; a poetic line witnesses وسق as gathering.

QASHANI:84:16-21/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:84:16-21/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:84:16-21/r2.claim: The body’s dark night gathers powers, instruments, and readinesses through which a person may gain knowledge, virtues, stations, gifts, and perfections.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r5.claim: Wasaq means gathered and joined; a wasq is sixty measures, and the word also describes collected food and gathered camels.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r6.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the moon's ittisaq is its fullness and evenness on the nights of the full moon, derived from gathering; muttasiq also means orderly.

SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r1.claim: In ‘wa-ma wasaq’, ‘ma’ may be a relative noun, a relative particle, or an indefinite; wasaq means gathering, as in a wasq measure of sixty ṣa‘s.

SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r2.claim: Wasaq with kasra is the noun and with fatḥa the verbal noun; food described as mawsuq is gathered, from the verbs wasaqa, ittasaqa, and istawsaqa.

SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r3.claim: Another sense of wasaq is that something acted upon or covered; a poem calls a camel-like force ‘al-wasiq al-mutalabbib’, and a rajaz line describes camels as mustawsiqa.

SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r4.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:84:17/r4.claim: Al-Farra’ says ‘idha ittasaq’ means the moon filled out and became even on full-moon nights; ittisaq is derived from the gathering sense of wasq.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p358/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p358/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p358/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Qatadah gloss ما وسق as what night gathers; Qatadah specifies stars and animals.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p358/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p358/r11.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p358/r11.claim: Ikrimah says night gathers by driving everything to its shelter with darkness.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.claim: Al-Inshiqāq continues the close of al-Muṭaffifīn: allies enjoy reward and enemies receive punishment because they denied resurrection and judgment before their Creator-King.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p372#s084/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p372#s084/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p372#s084/r3.claim: Night overcomes and removes twilight; what it gathers includes everything in its darkness, such as twilight, the preceding day, and stars, evidencing its Creator’s power to originate and resurrect.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p372#s084/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p372#s084/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p372#s084/r5.claim: These immense signs and benefits demonstrate God’s complete power to restore things exactly as they were; the resurrection claim is so evident that it needs no supporting oath.

BURSEVI:v10p294/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p294/r8.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p294/r8.claim: Wasaq is gathering scattered things; what night gathers includes animals and creatures returning to their shelters, or alternatively worshippers praying and seeking forgiveness before dawn.

ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r21.claim: Wasq means to gather, collect, accumulate, or load; the night’s gathering is what it collects, while ittiṣāq denotes orderly arrangement.

TABATABAI:84:16-24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:16-24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:16-24/r2.claim: The night gathers people and animals that spread out by day and return to their homes to rest; an alternative takes wasaq as driving stars from concealment into view.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p238/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p238/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p238/r1.claim: Physical phenomena show gradual change under God's control; humanity too steadily moves toward meeting its Lord, so denying that outcome is foolish.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r10.claim: Twilight, night, and the full moon represent changing conditions of light and darkness; their oaths stress human transitions in worldly life and at Resurrection and their cosmic relation.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r15.claim: All these changes prove resurrection is possible and that people ought to believe in it.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r8.claim: What the night gathers includes sights in the dark sky and every good or bad act and event made possible by night.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.claim: Al-Inshiqāq begins with human toil and successive ordeals, whereas al-Tīn begins by honoring humanity; its fa therefore suits the emphasis on continuing, unclouded reward.

STUDYQURAN:84:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:84:17/r1.claim: Tasaqa conveys gathering together like a herd; night symbolically gathers all in darkness as all will ultimately return to God.
